items.label: HTRANS Legality
items.description: Have you verified that HTRANS never transitions from BUSY to IDLE directly during a burst, and that a master does not change control signals while HREADY is low?

items.label: Wrap Boundary Calculation
items.description: Does the slave correctly calculate the wrap boundary for WRAP4, WRAP8, and WRAP16 bursts, returning the address to the lower bound rather than overflowing?

items.label: No Combinatorial HREADY Loops
items.description: Have you ensured that there are no combinatorial paths from HREADYIN to HREADYOUT in the slaves that could cause a combinatorial loop across the interconnect?

items.label: Two-Cycle ERROR Response
items.description: Do all slaves correctly hold HRESP=ERROR and HREADY=0 for the first cycle, and HRESP=ERROR and HREADY=1 for the second cycle when asserting an error?

items.label: Master Error Abort
items.description: Do all masters correctly abort the current burst by driving HTRANS=IDLE upon receiving a two-cycle ERROR response?

items.label: Arbitration Fairness
items.description: Under high traffic conditions, does the Arbiter (or interconnect matrix) guarantee that lower-priority masters eventually receive a grant (no starvation)?

items.label: Exclusive Access Monitor
items.description: If using AHB5, does the Exclusive Monitor correctly track addresses per master ID and correctly clear the monitor state when a different master writes to the watched address?

items.label: Secure Isolation (HNONSEC)
items.description: If using AHB5, do secure slaves explicitly reject Non-Secure (HNONSEC=1) transfers with an ERROR response, even if the address falls within their memory map?
